goals.title: Get 1 customer
goals.reasoning: Getting a first customer requires identifying a target audience, preparing a basic offer or product to sell, doing direct outreach, and closing the deal. I split this into sequential steps so the team isn't doing outreach before something is ready to sell, but kept the tasks broad enough that a human leader can fill in the specific product or market details. I left out scaling, marketing campaigns, and retention since the goal is strictly to land one customer.

proposed_tasks.title: Define the specific target customer profile (who they are, what problem they have, and what they'd pay for) and write a one-page summary the team can use for outreach.
Prepare a minimal viable offer or product package that can be delivered to a first customer, including pricing and what's included.
Build a list of 20-30 potential customers that match the target profile, including names, contact info, and a one-line reason why they'd be interested.
Draft a short outreach message and follow-up template tailored to the target profile, ready to be sent via email, WhatsApp, or LinkedIn.
Send outreach messages to the prospect list and track responses in a simple spreadsheet (sent, opened, replied, interested).
Follow up with interested prospects, answer their questions, and negotiate terms until at least one customer agrees to buy.
Onboard the first customer: send any welcome materials, collect payment, and confirm delivery details so the sale is completed.

goals.title: Lets build 10,000 units of ABION node City
goals.reasoning: Building 10,000 ABION node City units is a large-scale production goal, so I split it into a logical production pipeline: sourcing materials, finalizing the unit design/spec, setting up the manufacturing line, executing production in batches, implementing quality control, and coordinating logistics/distribution. I left out sales and post-deployment support since the goal is specifically about building the units, not selling or maintaining them. No specific person was named in the goal, so all assignees are left blank for the leader to assign based on capacity.

proposed_tasks.title: Source and secure all raw materials, components, and parts needed to manufacture 10,000 ABION node City units, including negotiating bulk pricing and confirming supplier delivery timelines.
Finalize the technical design and manufacturing spec for each ABION node City unit — including assembly diagrams, bill of materials, and step-by-step build instructions for the production team.
Set up the physical manufacturing line or assembly workspace: tools, workstations, staging areas for components, and any jigs or molds needed for efficient unit production.
Recruit, brief, and train the assembly workforce on the ABION node City build process, safety protocols, and daily production targets to ensure throughput of approximately 500 units per day.
Execute the full production run of 10,000 ABION node City units in managed batches, tracking daily output against the target and reporting any bottlenecks or material shortages immediately.

Establish and run a quality control checkpoint that tests each completed unit for functionality, firmware loading, and physical integrity before it leaves the production line; reject and route defective units for rework.

Coordinate storage, packaging, and distribution logistics for the finished 10,000 units — including warehouse space, packing materials, shipping manifests, and handoff to deployment or delivery teams.

knowledge_base.title: ABION City Node
knowledge_base.content:
An ABION City Node is a planned physical mini-city consisting of five buildings arranged as the ABION architectural symbol represented in the ABION Industries logo.

The standard ABION City Node contains 100 total floors distributed across five buildings:

Central Tower — 30 floors
Inner Tower 2 — 20 floors
Inner Tower 3 — 20 floors
Outer Tower 4 — 15 floors
Outer Tower 5 — 15 floors

Total: 5 buildings / 100 floors.

The five-building arrangement follows the visual composition of the ABION Industries logo: a dominant central tower surrounded by four progressively shorter towers. The logo therefore serves as the architectural identity and visual representation of the ABION City Node.

An ABION City Node is intended to function as a compact vertical mini-city, with its 100 floors potentially accommodating multiple functions and activities within a single integrated development. Specific floor-by-floor uses are to be defined separately.

Structure:
5 buildings · 100 floors · 30 + 20 + 20 + 15 + 15

Architectural Identity:
The five-building configuration is derived from the ABION Industries logo.

Here is the outreach message template:

---

Subject: Quick idea for [Company Name]

Hi [First Name],

I came across [Company Name] and noticed [specific observation about their business, recent news, or challenge]. It got me thinking about how we might help.

We help companies like yours [specific value proposition — e.g., reduce customer acquisition costs by 30%, streamline operations with automation, scale revenue without scaling headcount]. Recently, we worked with [similar company or industry example] and achieved [brief, credible result].

I'd like to share a few ideas specific to [Company Name] — no pitch, just a practical conversation about what might work for you.

Do you have 15-30 minutes this week? I'm flexible on days and times. If this week is tight, I'm happy to find a slot that works better for you.

Best,
[Your Name]
[Your Title]
[Your Company]
[Contact Information]

---

Usage notes for Femi:

- Keep the subject line under 50 characters when possible for better open rates.
- Replace every bracketed placeholder with prospect-specific details before sending. Generic templates get ignored.
- The observation line should reference something real — a recent hire, product launch, funding round, LinkedIn post, or industry trend. This proves the message is not batch-sent.
- The value proposition should be one sentence maximum. Focus on the outcome, not the process.
- The example result should be specific and verifiable. If you cannot share a real number, use a qualitative result instead.
- Send Tuesday through Thursday between 9-11 AM recipient local time for best response rates.
- Follow up once after 3 business days if no response. Do not send more than two follow-ups.
